column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4), Table 3 row 7: October 2026 index 120.50, +7.18% on a year, now read at source; NUMBERS 8d still carries September's +7.29% until the numbers owner updates it.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4): five years to October run 3.19% a year (reproduced on the register's own series plus 120.50); 8d and SKELETON 3e still say 3.27% to September until the numbers owner updates them; band stands.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4) watch line: the 7% headline is mostly Dec 2025 to May 2026 (+5.24%); May to Oct +1.46%, about 3.5% a year, inside the band (reproduced); October's reading, so 8d's update caveat applies.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: a 12-month rise above 7.18% in 73 of 418 months (reproduced); overlapping windows; the 2.5% threshold is public-contract law, context only.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: three-year index rises above 20% in 15.2% of 394 windows (reproduced); index history, never a facility cost estimate; 8q already tests the joint two-year move.

Tue 17 Nov: Store: under the model clause the owner carries the excess above 2.5%, at most 65% of a 7.18% rise; corrects the store's 'pass index rises to the owner' (H3-072, Q5e-011) for public contracts.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the PCC's worked example behind row 6; my recompute gives about NT$1,254,950 against the PCC's NT$1,255,007, a rounding gap in the source.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the 2004 relief applied only where the project's own budget could cover it; Taiwan administrative rule, context for the half kept, never legal analysis.

Tue 17 Nov: 3b/3e store: Taiwan's 2004, 2008 and 2009 burst-relief rules excluded subsidised legal persons and groups by name, so a co-sponsored residency meets a burst with its own spare money; context only, legal requirements are outside the case (l.168-169).
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the 2008 subsidy principle's dates and thresholds, read through Rootlaw's copy; relief as a dated exception.

Tue 17 Nov: 3b parallel for the half kept: in 2008 the government paid a burst from the job's own savings and budget first; the break (a government can tax and borrow, Laura has two reasons only) travels with it; co-sponsors still exist, so drop 'nothing behind it'.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: cutting the work is a named lever in the 2008 list; the residency's design choices are its own and outside the case, so never a plan step.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the 2008 relief's duties and closing dates; administrative detail.
Tue 17 Nov: Store/3e: bursts are fast (reproduced), but one quarter (+11.6%, Dec 2003 to Mar 2004) is more than two years of the band's 5% top, not three; one year (+16.5%) carried more than three.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: relief rules reached back after a burst, so until they came a budget carried it alone; public works only.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the clause refunds owners in a fall, which is why the 2009 waiver was born; adds the reason to Q10e-027's date.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: restoring a clause reaches only work not yet done, already in Q10e-028; the 30 Dec 2021 end of waivers is in Q10e-029.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: in 2021 the PCC's answer was more clauses, not a subsidy; the absence of a relief rule rests on the pages searched.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the model clause's default named items; public contracts only.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the relief principles are administrative rules that cannot change a private contract; with Q10e-031, the contract decides who carries a rise.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: past relief covered domestic materials only, so imported fit-out sits outside an index clause; one article's suggestion, and the national index is not her building (8q limits).
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Civil Code art. 227-2's text, read at source; the floor under every fixed price in Taiwan; context only, never legal advice.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: courts split on whether a no-adjustment clause shuts out art. 227-2; read only as quoted by one article.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Chiayi City Hall's 2004 burst split in halves after years in court; the remand ruling was not read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: an index clause can miss one material (Taipower, owner bore about 63% of the gap, checked: 51.09 of 81.23); a state utility, not a residency.
Tue 17 Nov: Store only; the conceit use is refused: a judgment is a figure owed, and ink is a figure owned in Treasuries (a pledge is owed, her floor owned).
Tue 17 Nov: Store: art. 227-2 claims should be made quickly, and owner-caused delay turns design changes into a price claim; public road case.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: 2008 relief paid to a main contractor did not reach its steel subcontractor; outside anything the case asks.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the private-subcontract dismissal is in Q10e-029; carry the late site and the private-contract argument as detail.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: a waived clause stays waived (Kinmen 2025), about 1% a month held foreseeable.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4) and Table 3 row 7 presentation: quote every index move as a percentage with its data month (the Kinmen claim's 11.49 was points; 11.80% checked).
Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 7 presentation: DGBAS's own rules for index-linked figures (data month, percentage, threshold); pairs with row 31.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: under the NLMA's points who causes a delay carries the index during it; one agency.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: 427 adjusted contracts ended 2017 to Jul 2022, NT$1.576bn; with Q10c-016 and Q10c-010 (2021 materials-led, 2026 wage-led).

Tue 17 Nov: Store: the Green Museumbrary's three failed tenders came in 2018, when the index rose only about 2.8% (Dec to Dec, register series), so not a burst; say price risk before signing sits with the owner, never that a burst showed as no bidders.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: its clause paid about 2.4% of the contract while the index rose 22.4% (reproduced); final total not found and much work came later.

Tue 17 Nov: Store, 3b background: a Taiwan arts building met the 2021-22 burst with about a seventh more money from its owner; a large public building is the wrong reference class (as Q9-027) and never a sizing of her overrun.

Tue 17 Nov: Store: the Interior Ministry's private renovation template has a fixed price and no adjustment clause; with Q10e-031, corrects the store's 'contracts pass rises to the owner' for private fit-out.
Tue 17 Nov: Store only: never call her flexibility insurance; no premium, a private contract may have no clause, and her shares do not move with building costs.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: art. 227-2 follows Germany's lost-basis doctrine (BGB 313); academic background only.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the 2008 channel parts add to $455m against a $395m total (CONFLICTING); use only the 2006-07 split or the total.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: in 2009 comic shops' graphic novels fell 15% while BookScan's line fell 8% in 25 weeks; collectors' channel hit hardest.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2): her genre fell a year after the 2008 crash, about three times as fast as all books (BookScan units -9.3% and -13.9% against -3.3% and -4.5%); the case's own genre for l.9's 'later', in place of Q12-018's 2023 figure; same downturn, later, never a lag or beta.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e store: BookScan's top 750 confirms Q12b-001 on a second dataset (manga -21.5%, the rest +18.8% in 2009; about +14% without Watchmen, Keel arithmetic); book sales, never evidence against l.9's 'smaller', which is about advances, fees and licences.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Graphix rose 24.8% in 2009 and fell 16.4% in 2010 (checked), a release calendar not the economy; the case never says her books are children's.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: 2009's release cut was manga's; non-manga releases -2.2% (checked); lists outside manga barely shrank.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2) store: in 2007-10 listed titles rose 67% and sales per title fell 53% (checked), the figure advances follow (row 29), so the squeeze reached new advances, not the shelf.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the same pattern in 2023 (titles +6.8%, sales per title -20%, checked); pairs with row 7.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e/2.3: I agree with Q108 that Q12-018's 'her genre fell by a third' was mostly manga: in 2023 manga lost 7.74m of the whole list's 7.87m units (Keel arithmetic on this row) while the non-manga long tail fell 0.6%; GEM_LEDGER row 3's 3e clause needs this fix.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e/2.3: agree the -22.4% and -11.5% were mostly manga with YA hits in 2024; fix the card's own wording too: the third is BookScan's adult graphic novel line, while the whole list fell 15.0% in 2023 (row 8), so never 'graphic novels as BookScan counts them fell about a third'; whether the YA fall sits inside the adult line is not shown.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the slump ended within two years in a rising market, 2025 a record $2.2bn; two BookScan scopes move differently.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: channel splits 2019-2024 extend Q12b-002's totals; methods changed in 2020, 2023 and 2024.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: 2020's growth through other doors while Diamond shut seven weeks adds detail to Q12b-002 and CANON B4's 2020 rise; a closure, not a recession.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the genre's long boom ($75m in 2001 to $395m in 2008) hides its dips; the pitch's 'giant stock' as a single stock, never a forecast of her genre's growth.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Tokyopop cut its list and reopened licences together, months before Lehman, warned by bookshop returns; a manga licensor, not an author's publisher.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: a retailer's failure (Borders, 2011, S&P +2.10%) stopped money already earned; pairs with Q12-011 (authors' royalties unpaid) and row 31.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: DC closed Minx for shelving, not the economy, taking a creator's finished book; launch spend CONFLICTING.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Virgin Comics became Liquid Comics; an end can be a change of owner.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the imprint closures were manga lines, two to three years after the share trough; supports 'later' at most as background.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Diamond raised its minimum order in Jan 2009 citing the economy; reached small presses, not advances.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: marketing went before books at BookExpo 2009; one show.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: ICv2's reasons for 2009's fall (shelf space, store closures, selective buying); an analyst's reading, with row 3.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 store beside Laura's own line (goldmine row 36): fix the figure: 837 is the average across all 53,466 listed titles (44.74m / 53,466, row 8), not the top 750; quote her line once, never about the case's money.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Scholastic's FY2023 trade fell while book fairs rose 29%; book fairs are family money at school (Q12b-008), background only.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: the 2023-24 cuts were firm-specific (IDW, Oni, Abrams), idiosyncratic risk like a single stock's.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: imprints opened in the 2023-24 slump, killing 'lists and imprints go first'; 23rd Street's launch month seen in headlines only.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2) store: new deals fell first (children's deals -17% in Q2 2024) while the top set records; market-wide, open excerpts only, and the case never says her books are children's, so never 'her corner of the market'.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: 192 graphic novel deals in 2023 against about 137 agents; a small deal market.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: a graphic novel advance follows expected sales, not work, and signing to release runs about a year; one agent and one editor.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2): IPS l.9 says advances come later and smaller, so drop 'less their size'; say new deals fall first and money comes later; Laura's contracts are not known (Keel inference).

Tue 17 Nov: 3e/2.3 store: her genre's sharpest cash shock (Diamond's Chapter 11, Jan 2025, S&P 2024 +24.88%) came from its own pipes, the single-stock reading of the pitch; never 'her career moves against shares'.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: comic shops led the 2025 recovery; about 125 stores behind the estimate.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2): twin of row 3 with the S&P years and ICv2's 2013 'tough couple of years' quote; carry the quote, say same downturn, later; Borders and manga are causes of their own.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: Australia's kids' and literary graphic novels rose in 2023; Australian angle only if it earns its place.
Tue 17 Nov: Store: kids' graphic novels were the steadiest part of the genre, dominated by Dog Man; the case says read in classrooms, never that her books are children's.
